claim: On January 5, 2016, Hollywood producer Barry Josephson (Josephson Entertainment) emailed Jeffrey Epstein under the subject line "Dr. Agus" — a single line: "All you need is a blood transfusion fr=m the pack and you reverse aging!!" (the "=" is quoted-printable encoding damage in the DOJ release; the line reads "from the pack"). The email was released by the Department of Justice in 2026 as document EFTA01801501 (Bates EFTA_R1_00142502) in DataSet 10 of the Epstein Files Transparency Act production. January 2016 is the period when young-blood plasma research (parabiosis) was widely covered in the press. In 2019 the New York Times reported Epstein's fascination with transhumanism and life extension, including telling an adherent of transhumanism that on his death he wanted his head and penis cryonically frozen. No reply to the Josephson email appears in the released production, and it is the only occurrence of the phrase in the release.

sources.label: The New York Times — "Jeffrey Epstein Hoped to Seed Human Race With His DNA" (July 31, 2019), reporting his transhumanism and life-extension fascination.

notes: Found by exact-phrase search over the full extracted-text corpus (work/corpus.jsonl, ~503K DS10 docs): the phrase appears exactly once in the entire release. "Dr. Agus" is read as David Agus (USC oncologist/media physician) — plausible given the subject line and the 2016 anti-aging news cycle, but the email itself doesn't expand the name, so the claim doesn't assert the identification. "The pack" presumably references whatever Agus segment/article prompted the email; no antecedent is in the released thread. Sender redactions (email address, phone) are DOJ's, preserved as released. The hosted PDF is a verbatim copy of the released file. Verify gate caught one drift during drafting: the NYT 2019 article documents cryonics/transhumanism, NOT young-blood transfusions — an earlier draft misattributed young-blood interest to it; corrected to what the article actually reports.
